facts.statement: The holotype of Teratosaurus was discovered in 1860 by Sixt Friedrich Jakob von Kapff near Stuttgart, Germany.
facts.quote: In 1860, Sixt Friedrich Jakob von Kapff at the Heslacher Wand near Stuttgart discovered the upper jaw bone of a large reptile.

facts.statement: The genus name Teratosaurus comes from Greek words meaning 'monster' and 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek τέρας, teras, "[ominous birth of a] monster" and sauros, "lizard".

facts.statement: The holotype fossil suggests the animal reached a body length of about six meters.
facts.quote: It indicates a body length of about six metres.

facts.statement: Early researchers incorrectly assigned fossils of the sauropodomorph dinosaur Efraasia to Teratosaurus.
facts.quote: Later authors, such as Kapff himself, von Huene, Osborn, and Edwin H. Colbert, incorrectly attributed postcrania of the sauropodomorph dinosaur Efraasia to this species or genus

facts.statement: For much of the 20th century, Teratosaurus was mistakenly believed to be a large, bipedal meat-eating dinosaur.
facts.quote: Following this lead, many popular books in the 20th century depicted "teratosaurs" as the earliest sort of large-bodied meat-eating dinosaur, walking on two legs and preying on the prosauropods of its day.

facts.statement: Many scientists once thought Teratosaurus was an ancestor of the Jurassic carnosaurs.
facts.quote: It was thought by many to be a Triassic ancestor to the "carnosaurs" of the Jurassic.

facts.statement: Research in 1985 and 1986 proved Teratosaurus was a rauisuchian, a four-legged predatory archosaur that lived alongside dinosaurs.
facts.quote: In 1985 and 1986, Peter Galton and Michael Benton independently showed that Teratosaurus is actually a rauisuchian, a type of non-dinosaurian large predatory archosaur, many of which walked on all fours, and lived alongside dinosaurs during the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: The species Teratosaurus silesiacus was moved to the genus Polonosuchus in 2009.
facts.quote: Teratosaurus silesiacus, described in 2005 by Tomasz Sulej on the basis of a left maxilla, was transferred to the genus Polonosuchus by Brussatte et al. in 2009.

facts.statement: Teratosaurus lived between 251.902 and 205.7 million years ago, from the Induan to the Norian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Induan to Norian (251.902 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Teratosaurus belongs to the order Rauisuchia.
Teratosaurus is classified within the family Rauisuchidae.

rejected.statement: The holotype is a 245-millimeter-long right upper jawbone containing six teeth up to five centimeters long.
rejected.quote: The holotype, specimen NHMUK PV OR 38646, was found in the Mittlerer Stubensandstein. It consists of a 245 millimetres long right maxilla with six large, up to five centimetres long, teeth.
